questions.q: A block of metal weighing 2 kg is resting on a frictionless plane (as shown in figure). It is struck by a jet releasing water at a rate of 1 kg s-1 and at a speed of 10 m s-1. Then, the initial acceleration of the block, in m s-2, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let velocity of water jet be v.

So, force applied is F=ΔpΔt=∆mvΔt

⇒ma=∆mvΔt

Acceleration of block, a=1×102

a=5 m s-2

questions.q: A block of 3 kg is attached to a string whose other end is attached to the wall. An unknown force F is applied so that the string makes an angle of 30° with the wall. The tension T is : (Given g =10 m s–2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From geometry, θ=30°.

For equilibrium,

Tcosθ=mg

⇒T=mgcos30°⇒T=3×1032

⇒T=20 N

questions.q: A heavy box of mass $50 \mathrm{~kg}$ is moving on a horizontal surface. If co-efficient of kinetic friction between the box and horizontal surface is 0.3 then force of kinetic friction is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $F_k=\mu_k N=0.3 \times 50 \times 9.8=147 N$

questions.q: A uniform metal chain of mass m and length L passes over a massless and frictionless pulley. It is released from rest with a part of its length l is hanging on one side and rest of its length L-l is hanging on the other side of the pulley. At a certain point of time, when l=Lx, the acceleration of the chain is g2. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the information given in the question, the part of the chain that envelopes the pulley is very small. Therefore, the acceleration of the chain can be written as,

a=m2-m1m2+m1g

Since a=g2

g2=m2-m1m2+m1g⇒g2=L-l-lLg⇒l=L4=Lx

⇒x=4

questions.q: A light string passing over a smooth light fixed pulley connects two blocks of masses m1 and m2. If the acceleration of the system is g8, then the ratio of masses is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the system can be written as, a=m1-m2gm1+m2=g8

⇒8m1-8m2=m1+m2

⇒7m1=9m2

⇒m1m2=97

questions.q: A given object takes $\mathrm{n}$ times the time to slide down $45^{\circ}$ rough inclined plane as it takes the time to slide down an identical perfectly smooth $45^{\circ}$ inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of inclined plane is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Case-1 : No friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta) \mathrm{t}_1^2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \end{aligned}$ Case-2 : With friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta) \mathrm{t}_2^2 \\ & \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu g \cos \theta}}=\mathrm{n} \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \\ & \mu=1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^2} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two billiard balls of equal mass 30 g strike a rigid wall with same speed of 108 kmph (as shown) but at different angles. If the balls get reflected with the same speed, then the ratio of the magnitude of impulses imparted to ball a and ball b by the wall along X direction is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Impulse = change in momentum

Ball (a) |Δp→|=2mu=J1

Ball (b) |Δp→|=2mucos45°=J2

J1 J2=1cos45°=2

questions.q: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> slides down the plane inclined at angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with an acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>g</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> . The value of coefficient of kinetic friction will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Newton's second law along the direction perpendicular to inlined plane:

N-mgcos30∘=0 (As θ=30°)

(since the acceleration of block in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane is 0)

∴N=mgcos30∘   .....(1)

Let μ be the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the inclined plane. Applying Newton's second law along inclined plane:

mgsin30∘-μN=ma=mg4    ....(2)

(since the acceleration along the inclined plane, a=g4)

∴mgsin30∘-μmgcos30∘=mg4   (from equation 1 and 2)

⇒mg2-32μmg=mg4

⇒μ=123

questions.q: As per given figure, a weightless pulley P is attached on a double inclined frictionless surface. The tension in the string (massless) will be (if g=10 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnitude of acceleration of both the blocks will be same and is given by

a=4 g sin 60∘-g sin 30∘4+1

=203-55

a=43-1 m s-1

Applying Newton's second law for second block (along the direction parallel to the incline on which it is placed)

T-5=1×a

⇒T=5+43-1

=43+1 N

questions.q:
The initial mass of a rocket is 1000 kg. Calculate at what rate the fuel should be burnt so that the rocket is given an acceleration of, 20 m s-2. The gases come out at a relative speed of 500 m s-1, with respect to the rocket:

Use g=10 m s-2
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here we are applying the equation, Fr−mg=ma

From Newton's second law, Fr=dmdtvr⇒dmdtvr=mg+ma

Put the given values in the above equations, 

⇒dmdt500=1000(10+20)⇒dmdt=60 kg s-1.

questions.q: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> starts sliding on a surface with an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The coefficient of friction between the surface and block is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The distance covered by the block before coming to rest is :[use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given initial velocity u=9.8 m s-1.

Acceleration a=μg=0.5×9.8=4.9 m s-2

Using, v2=u2+2as, here, final velocity v=0.

So, 0=9.82+24.9s⇒s=9.8 m

questions.q: A modern grand-prix racing car of mass m is travelling on a flat track in a circular arc of radius R with a speed v. If the coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the track is μs, then the magnitude of negative lift FL acting downwards on the car is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
μsN=mv2R

N=mv2μsR=mg+FL

FL=mv2μsR-mg

questions.q: A wooden block, initially at rest on the ground, is pushed by a force which increases linearly with time $t$. Which of the following curve best describes acceleration of the block with time:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma} \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{kt}}{\mathrm{m}}$ a vs $t$ will be straight line passing through origin.

questions.q:
The figure represents the momentum time (p-t) curve for a particle moving along an axis under the influence of the force. Identify the regions on the graph where the magnitude of the force is maximum and minimum respectively ?

If t3-t2<t1

questions.solution:
From Newton's second,

F=dpdt=slope of p-t curve

questions.q: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is placed at rest on a table of rough surface. Now, if a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> is applied in the direction parallel to surface of the table, the block slides through a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> in an interval of time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. Coefficient of kinetic friction is (given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Forces acting on block is shown below

From the second equation of motion,

s=12at2⇒50=12a×102⇒a=1 m s-2

Applying Newton's second law in vertical direction,

R-mg=0⇒R=mg

(where R is the magnitude of normal reaction on the block due to the surface)

If μ is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface, applying Newton's second law in horizontal direction,

30-μR=ma⇒30-μmg=ma⇒30-50μ=5⇒μ=12=0.5

questions.q: A balloon has mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> in air. The air escapes from the balloon at a uniform rate with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the balloon shrinks in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> completely. Then, the average force acting on that balloon will be (in dyne).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that the mass of the air m=10 g and it escapes in time t=5 s with velocity v=4.5 cm s-1.

The average force on the balloon can be given as,

F=vdmdt

⇒F=4.5×105=9 dyne

questions.q: Consider a block and trolley system as shown in figure. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the trolley and the surface is 0.04, the acceleration of the system in m s-2 is: (Consider that the string is massless and unstretchable and the pulley is also massless and frictionless) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum kinetic friction acting, fk=μN=0.04×20g=8 Newton

Therefore, acceleration of the system will bea=60−826=2 m s-2

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> moves along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis such that it's velocity varies with displacement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> according to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> the force acting on the body is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that 

 v=10x m s-1

Force is defined by F=mdvdt   ...(i)

Multiplying and dividing equation (i) by dx

F=mdvdtdxdx⇒F=mdxdtdvdx=mvdvdx   ...(ii)

Finding the values of the terms in equation (ii)
dvdx=102x=5x
vdvdx=a=10x×5x=50 m s-2

Hence, the force is 
F=12×50=25 N.

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is moving with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The body stops after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> due to friction between body and the floor. The value of the coefficient of friction is: (Take acceleration due to gravity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Friction force wil act opposite to the motion of the body.

F=μN=μmg

⇒a=-μg-ve sign for direction relative to the motion of body

Now, applying equation of motion, we get

v=u+at

⇒0=20+-μ×10×5

⇒50μ=20

 ⇒μ=0.4

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> experiences two forces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover></math> The acceleration acting on the body is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force F→=F→1+F→2=8i^+4j^+4k^

Therefore, required acceleration a→=F→m=2i^+j^+k^

questions.q: A uniform chain of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The co-efficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, the maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let, λ=mass per unit length of the chain and length of mass hanging through the table is x.

Normal force applied by the table on the chain will be, N=l-xλg.

Tension developed in the chain will balance the gravitational force acting in the downward direction, T=λxg.

Maximum limiting force possible for the part of the table, fmax=μN=μl-xλg

For equilibrium,

fmax=T,

⇒μl-xλg=λxg⇒12×6-x=x ⇒x=2 m
